doc.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Prices of movies, vaudeville and club dates
summary: Movie and vaudeville ticket prices, and a comparison with what young players earn on club dates today.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: How much did it cost to get into the movies when you were a kid?

Oh gee, well now we used to call it a nickelette. So that was just the movies. But a vaudeville show was probably about 25 or 30 cents or something. I know it’s hard to believe. Well whenever anybody says — you know these young fellas, they go out and they do these club dates, and I says well how— He says you’ll never get, like you can’t earn a living. I says well how much do you get when you do these? Well he says $150. And they’ve got two or three over the weekend. I says that’s quite a lot. They says no, that ain’t no good, you get with the big offices, you do good. You know he says they’re gypping me. So I don’t know what to say. So I tell them, I says lookit, when I was young, what was a postal stamp? Not so far back, like two cents, right? Then it went up to three cents, everybody went wild. Now, 32 cents. That’s the difference with your money.
